## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

# Connect Supabase Cloud + Migrate Schema + Prune Test Deps

## Context

InkOS finished Sprint 12 against a local Supabase (or empty cloud). Shipping to Railway requires a linked cloud project so migrations, auth, storage, and types point at a real database. The user provided:

- Project URL: `https://lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb.supabase.co`
- Publishable key: `sb_publishable_OORu8axEG5vnGH2VByhO0w_lQK_DR6i`

The cloud target is empty. We need to link, push all 19 migrations (15,401 lines across [supabase/migrations/](supabase/migrations/)), regenerate types, and update `.env.local`.

Separately, dev deps carry three libraries that are installed but never actually exercised by the current test suite: `msw` (no handlers), `@vitest/ui` (only wired through the `test:ui` script), and `@testing-library/jest-dom` (imported in [tests/setup.ts](tests/setup.ts) but none of the 3 unit tests use its matchers — all three are pure-logic tests). Removing them cuts install time and devDep surface with zero risk to the suite.

`@supabase/ssr` and `@supabase/supabase-js` are **already installed** ([package.json:44-45](package.json#L44-L45)) — the `npm install` step from the pasted Supabase snippet is a no-op and will be skipped.

Env var name stays `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` (the new `sb_publishable_*` value is format-compatible; renaming would touch 6+ files and [lib/env.ts](lib/env.ts) validator).

---

## Part 1 — Connect Supabase Cloud

### 1.1 Update [.env.local](.env.local)

Set (create file if missing):

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=sb_publishable_OORu8axEG5vnGH2VByhO0w_lQK_DR6i
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<user-provides — from Supabase Dashboard → Settings → API → service_role>
SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD=<user-provides — from Supabase Dashboard → Settings → Database>
SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET=<user-provides — from Supabase Dashboard → Settings → API → JWT Secret>
```

Leave the rest of `.env.local` (Dodo, Resend, Sentry, Upstash, etc.) as-is. User will confirm these three sensitive values are filled before we run migrations.

### 1.2 Link CLI to cloud project

```
pnpm dlx supabase login          # one-time; opens browser for access token
pnpm dlx supabase link --project-ref lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb
# Prompts for SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD
```

This writes `.supabase/` state locally (already in [.gitignore](.gitignore) via `supabase/.branches`/`.temp` — verify).

### 1.3 Push all 19 migrations

```
pnpm db:migrate                  # wraps `supabase db push`
```

This runs every migration in [supabase/migrations/](supabase/migrations/) in filename order against the cloud DB. Covers: bootstrap → platform admin → booking engine → CRM → billing → consent forms → commissions → payroll/tax → AI design → inventory → multilocation/white-label → launch hardening → audit fixes.

**No seed file exists** — skip `db:reset`. If seed data is needed later, Dato creates `supabase/seed.sql`.

### 1.4 Regenerate typed schema

```
pnpm db:types                    # supabase gen types typescript --linked > lib/supabase/types.ts
```

Overwrites the hand-written [lib/supabase/types.ts](lib/supabase/types.ts) with the real cloud schema. Run `pnpm typecheck` after to confirm nothing in the app broke against the regenerated types.

### 1.5 Post-connection config (in Supabase Dashboard, manual)

Required runtime settings the CLI can't push:

1. **Auth → URL Configuration** — add `http://localhost:3100` and the Railway prod URL to Redirect URLs.
2. **Auth → Email Templates** — keep defaults for now; Quill replaces in a later sprint.
3. **Database → Extensions** — confirm `pgcrypto`, `uuid-ossp`, `pg_trgm` are enabled (migrations expect them).
4. **Settings → Database → Set GUC** — run in SQL editor once: `ALTER DATABASE postgres SET app.settings.tin_encryption_key = '<TIN_ENCRYPTION_KEY>';` (only if payroll/W-9 flows will be tested; otherwise defer to pre-launch).

---

## Part 2 — Remove Unused Test Dependencies

### 2.1 Remove packages

```
pnpm remove msw @vitest/ui @testing-library/jest-dom
```

### 2.2 Update [tests/setup.ts](tests/setup.ts)

Delete line 1 (`import '@testing-library/jest-dom'`). Keep the rest (env var seeding). Confirmed safe: `grep toBeInTheDocument|toHaveClass|toHaveTextContent|toBeVisible|toBeDisabled|toHaveAttribute` across [tests/](tests/) returns zero hits — no test uses jest-dom matchers.

### 2.3 Update [package.json](package.json)

Remove the `test:ui` script (line 20) — it references the removed `@vitest/ui`. Keep `test`, `test:watch`, `test:coverage`, `test:e2e`. Playwright stays (user wants E2E capacity for future, even though [tests/e2e/](tests/e2e/) is currently empty).

---

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| [.env.local](.env.local) | Set Supabase URL + anon key (publishable); user fills service role / DB pw / JWT secret |
| [lib/supabase/types.ts](lib/supabase/types.ts) | Regenerated from cloud schema via `pnpm db:types` |
| [tests/setup.ts](tests/setup.ts) | Drop `@testing-library/jest-dom` import |
| [package.json](package.json) | Remove 3 devDeps + `test:ui` script |
| [pnpm-lock.yaml](pnpm-lock.yaml) | Auto-updated by `pnpm remove` |

No changes to [lib/env.ts](lib/env.ts), [lib/supabase/server.ts](lib/supabase/server.ts), [lib/supabase/client.ts](lib/supabase/client.ts), [lib/supabase/middleware.ts](lib/supabase/middleware.ts), [lib/supabase/public.ts](lib/supabase/public.ts), [proxy.ts](proxy.ts), [middleware.ts](middleware.ts) — they already reference the correct env var name.

---

## Verification

Run sequentially:

1. `pnpm install` — lockfile reconciles after removals
2. `pnpm typecheck` — confirms regenerated `lib/supabase/types.ts` is consistent with callers (DAL, server actions, API routes)
3. `pnpm test` — all 3 unit tests must still pass (utils, csv-sanitize, dodo-webhook-verify are pure logic, unaffected by jest-dom removal)
4. `pnpm dev` — start on port 3100
5. Visit `http://localhost:3100` → should redirect to `/login` (waitlist page lives at `/`; auth redirect comes from root middleware)
6. Sign up a test user at `/signup` → confirm row appears in Supabase Studio → `auth.users`
7. Complete `/onboarding` → confirm row in `studios` and `studio_members` (cloud)
8. Hit `/dashboard` → no runtime 500s, Sentry clean
9. `curl http://localhost:3100/api/health` → returns 200 with DB status OK

**Rollback path:** If `supabase db push` fails mid-way, the 19 migrations are idempotent by file but not by content — manually drop the `public` schema via Dashboard SQL editor (`DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA public;`) and re-run. Service role key is not required for migrations (CLI uses DB password).

---

## Out of Scope (explicit)

- Running `npx skills add supabase/agent-skills` — user can run this ad-hoc; no project-level effect
- Populating Dodo Payments / Resend / Sentry / Upstash secrets — separate task before Railway deploy
- Removing Playwright — user kept it for future E2E
- Writing new tests — suite stays as-is

|------|--------|
| Supabase CLI linked to cloud project `lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb` | ✅ |

## Types regen: reverted — and here's why (latent bug)

Ran `pnpm dlx supabase@latest gen types typescript --linked` successfully. But merging cloud schema into the codebase surfaced **real drift** between migrations and app code:

| Cloud column (from [supabase/migrations/20260416000008_inventory_guest_artist.sql](supabase/migrations/20260416000008_inventory_guest_artist.sql)) | App code + hand-written types | Affected files |
|---|---|---|
| `min_stock_threshold` | `min_threshold` | [components/inventory/ItemForm.tsx](components/inventory/ItemForm.tsx), [ItemsTable.tsx](components/inventory/ItemsTable.tsx) |
| `sell_price_cents` (only) | `retail_price_cents` | [ItemForm.tsx](components/inventory/ItemForm.tsx) |
| (missing) | `location_description` | [ItemForm.tsx](components/inventory/ItemForm.tsx) |
| (missing) | `qty_after` | [MovementsLog.tsx](components/inventory/MovementsLog.tsx) |
| text columns | `PayrollRunStatus` / `TaxFormStatus` strict unions | payroll components |

**Impact:** At runtime, Sprint 5 (inventory) and Sprint 8 (payroll) queries will return `undefined` for these fields. # Connect Supabase Cloud + Migrate Schema + Prune Test Deps

## Context

InkOS finished Sprint 12 against a local Supabase (or empty cloud). Shipping to Railway requires a linked cloud project so migrations, auth, storage, and types point at a real database. The user provided:

- Project URL: `https://lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb.supabase.co`
- Publishable key: `sb_publishable_OORu8axEG5vnGH2VByhO0w_lQK_DR6i`

The cloud target is empty. We need to link, push all 19 migrations (15,401 lines across [supabase/migrations/](supabase/migrations/)), regenerate types, and update `.env.local`.

Separately, dev deps carry three libraries that are installed but never actually exercised by the current test suite: `msw` (no handlers), `@vitest/ui` (only wired through the `test:ui` script), and `@testing-library/jest-dom` (imported in [tests/setup.ts](tests/setup.ts) but none of the 3 unit tests use its matchers — all three are pure-logic tests). Removing them cuts install time and devDep surface with zero risk to the suite.

`@supabase/ssr` and `@supabase/supabase-js` are **already installed** ([package.json:44-45](package.json#L44-L45)) — the `npm install` step from the pasted Supabase snippet is a no-op and will be skipped.

Env var name stays `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` (the new `sb_publishable_*` value is format-compatible; renaming would touch 6+ files and [lib/env.ts](lib/env.ts) validator).

---

## Part 1 — Connect Supabase Cloud

### 1.1 Update [.env.local](.env.local)

Set (create file if missing):

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=sb_publishable_OORu8axEG5vnGH2VByhO0w_lQK_DR6i
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<user-provides — from Supabase Dashboard → Settings → API → service_role>
SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD=<user-provides — from Supabase Dashboard → Settings → Database>
SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET=<user-provides — from Supabase Dashboard → Settings → API → JWT Secret>
```

Leave the rest of `.env.local` (Dodo, Resend, Sentry, Upstash, etc.) as-is. User will confirm these three sensitive values are filled before we run migrations.

### 1.2 Link CLI to cloud project

```
pnpm dlx supabase login          # one-time; opens browser for access token
pnpm dlx supabase link --project-ref lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb
# Prompts for SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD
```

This writes `.supabase/` state locally (already in [.gitignore](.gitignore) via `supabase/.branches`/`.temp` — verify).

### 1.3 Push all 19 migrations

```
pnpm db:migrate                  # wraps `supabase db push`
```

This runs every migration in [supabase/migrations/](supabase/migrations/) in filename order against the cloud DB. Covers: bootstrap → platform admin → booking engine → CRM → billing → consent forms → commissions → payroll/tax → AI design → inventory → multilocation/white-label → launch hardening → audit fixes.

**No seed file exists** — skip `db:reset`. If seed data is needed later, Dato creates `supabase/seed.sql`.

### 1.4 Regenerate typed schema

```
pnpm db:types                    # supabase gen types typescript --linked > lib/supabase/types.ts
```

Overwrites the hand-written [lib/supabase/types.ts](lib/supabase/types.ts) with the real cloud schema. Run `pnpm typecheck` after to confirm nothing in the app broke against the regenerated types.

### 1.5 Post-connection config (in Supabase Dashboard, manual)

Required runtime settings the CLI can't push:

1. **Auth → URL Configuration** — add `http://localhost:3100` and the Railway prod URL to Redirect URLs.
2. **Auth → Email Templates** — keep defaults for now; Quill replaces in a later sprint.
3. **Database → Extensions** — confirm `pgcrypto`, `uuid-ossp`, `pg_trgm` are enabled (migrations expect them).
4. **Settings → Database → Set GUC** — run in SQL editor once: `ALTER DATABASE postgres SET app.settings.tin_encryption_key = '<TIN_ENCRYPTION_KEY>';` (only if payroll/W-9 flows will be tested; otherwise defer to pre-launch).

---

## Part 2 — Remove Unused Test Dependencies

### 2.1 Remove packages

```
pnpm remove msw @vitest/ui @testing-library/jest-dom
```

### 2.2 Update [tests/setup.ts](tests/setup.ts)

Delete line 1 (`import '@testing-library/jest-dom'`). Keep the rest (env var seeding). Confirmed safe: `grep toBeInTheDocument|toHaveClass|toHaveTextContent|toBeVisible|toBeDisabled|toHaveAttribute` across [tests/](tests/) returns zero hits — no test uses jest-dom matchers.

### 2.3 Update [package.json](package.json)

Remove the `test:ui` script (line 20) — it references the removed `@vitest/ui`. Keep `test`, `test:watch`, `test:coverage`, `test:e2e`. Playwright stays (user wants E2E capacity for future, even though [tests/e2e/](tests/e2e/) is currently empty).

---

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| [.env.local](.env.local) | Set Supabase URL + anon key (publishable); user fills service role / DB pw / JWT secret |
| [lib/supabase/types.ts](lib/supabase/types.ts) | Regenerated from cloud schema via `pnpm db:types` |
| [tests/setup.ts](tests/setup.ts) | Drop `@testing-library/jest-dom` import |
| [package.json](package.json) | Remove 3 devDeps + `test:ui` script |
| [pnpm-lock.yaml](pnpm-lock.yaml) | Auto-updated by `pnpm remove` |

No changes to [lib/env.ts](lib/env.ts), [lib/supabase/server.ts](lib/supabase/server.ts), [lib/supabase/client.ts](lib/supabase/client.ts), [lib/supabase/middleware.ts](lib/supabase/middleware.ts), [lib/supabase/public.ts](lib/supabase/public.ts), [proxy.ts](proxy.ts), [middleware.ts](middleware.ts) — they already reference the correct env var name.

---

## Verification

Run sequentially:

1. `pnpm install` — lockfile reconciles after removals
2. `pnpm typecheck` — confirms regenerated `lib/supabase/types.ts` is consistent with callers (DAL, server actions, API routes)
3. `pnpm test` — all 3 unit tests must still pass (utils, csv-sanitize, dodo-webhook-verify are pure logic, unaffected by jest-dom removal)
4. `pnpm dev` — start on port 3100
5. Visit `http://localhost:3100` → should redirect to `/login` (waitlist page lives at `/`; auth redirect comes from root middleware)
6. Sign up a test user at `/signup` → confirm row appears in Supabase Studio → `auth.users`
7. Complete `/onboarding` → confirm row in `studios` and `studio_members` (cloud)
8. Hit `/dashboard` → no runtime 500s, Sentry clean
9. `curl http://localhost:3100/api/health` → returns 200 with DB status OK

**Rollback path:** If `supabase db push` fails mid-way, the 19 migrations are idempotent by file but not by content — manually drop the `public` schema via Dashboard SQL editor (`DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA public;`) and re-run. Service role key is not required for migrations (CLI uses DB password).

---

## Out of Scope (explicit)

- Running `npx skills add supabase/agent-skills` — user can run this ad-hoc; no project-level effect
- Populating Dodo Payments / Resend / Sentry / Upstash secrets — separate task before Railway deploy
- Removing Playwright — user kept it for future E2E
- Writing new tests — suite stays as-is

- ✅ [tests/setup.ts](tests/setup.ts) line 1 (`import '@testing-library/jest-dom'`) deleted
- ✅ [package.json](package.json) `test:ui` script deleted

|---|---|---|

```

Only `supabase/.branches/_current_branch` is currently committed (per `git ls-files supabase/` — `supabase/.temp/` is already gitignored, `supabase/snippets/` was never tracked). After the `rm` above:

```

Current state has `.supabase/` and `supabase/.temp/`. Add one line so `.branches/` doesn't get re-added if the CLI ever recreates it:

# add below `supabase/.temp/`:
supabase/.branches/
```

# Connect Supabase Cloud + Migrate Schema + Prune Test Deps

## Context

InkOS finished Sprint 12 against a local Supabase (or empty cloud). Shipping to Railway requires a linked cloud project so migrations, auth, storage, and types point at a real database. The user provided:

- Project URL: `https://lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb.supabase.co`
- Publishable key: `sb_publishable_OORu8axEG5vnGH2VByhO0w_lQK_DR6i`

The cloud target is empty. We need to link, push all 19 migrations (15,401 lines across [supabase/migrations/](supabase/migrations/)), regenerate types, and update `.env.local`.

Separately, dev deps carry three libraries that are installed but never actually exercised by the current test suite: `msw` (no handlers), `@vitest/ui` (only wired through the `test:ui` script), and `@testing-library/jest-dom` (imported in [tests/setup.ts](tests/setup.ts) but none of the 3 unit tests use its matchers — all three are pure-logic tests). Removing them cuts install time and devDep surface with zero risk to the suite.

`@supabase/ssr` and `@supabase/supabase-js` are **already installed** ([package.json:44-45](package.json#L44-L45)) — the `npm install` step from the pasted Supabase snippet is a no-op and will be skipped.

Env var name stays `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` (the new `sb_publishable_*` value is format-compatible; renaming would touch 6+ files and [lib/env.ts](lib/env.ts) validator).

---

## Part 1 — Connect Supabase Cloud

### 1.1 Update [.env.local](.env.local)

Set (create file if missing):

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=sb_publishable_OORu8axEG5vnGH2VByhO0w_lQK_DR6i
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<user-provides — from Supabase Dashboard → Settings → API → service_role>
SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD=<user-provides — from Supabase Dashboard → Settings → Database>
SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET=<user-provides — from Supabase Dashboard → Settings → API → JWT Secret>
```

Leave the rest of `.env.local` (Dodo, Resend, Sentry, Upstash, etc.) as-is. User will confirm these three sensitive values are filled before we run migrations.

### 1.2 Link CLI to cloud project

```
pnpm dlx supabase login          # one-time; opens browser for access token
pnpm dlx supabase link --project-ref lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb
# Prompts for SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD
```

This writes `.supabase/` state locally (already in [.gitignore](.gitignore) via `supabase/.branches`/`.temp` — verify).

### 1.3 Push all 19 migrations

```
pnpm db:migrate                  # wraps `supabase db push`
```

This runs every migration in [supabase/migrations/](supabase/migrations/) in filename order against the cloud DB. Covers: bootstrap → platform admin → booking engine → CRM → billing → consent forms → commissions → payroll/tax → AI design → inventory → multilocation/white-label → launch hardening → audit fixes.

**No seed file exists** — skip `db:reset`. If seed data is needed later, Dato creates `supabase/seed.sql`.

### 1.4 Regenerate typed schema

```
pnpm db:types                    # supabase gen types typescript --linked > lib/supabase/types.ts
```

Overwrites the hand-written [lib/supabase/types.ts](lib/supabase/types.ts) with the real cloud schema. Run `pnpm typecheck` after to confirm nothing in the app broke against the regenerated types.

### 1.5 Post-connection config (in Supabase Dashboard, manual)

Required runtime settings the CLI can't push:

1. **Auth → URL Configuration** — add `http://localhost:3100` and the Railway prod URL to Redirect URLs.
2. **Auth → Email Templates** — keep defaults for now; Quill replaces in a later sprint.
3. **Database → Extensions** — confirm `pgcrypto`, `uuid-ossp`, `pg_trgm` are enabled (migrations expect them).
4. **Settings → Database → Set GUC** — run in SQL editor once: `ALTER DATABASE postgres SET app.settings.tin_encryption_key = '<TIN_ENCRYPTION_KEY>';` (only if payroll/W-9 flows will be tested; otherwise defer to pre-launch).

---

## Part 2 — Remove Unused Test Dependencies

### 2.1 Remove packages

```
pnpm remove msw @vitest/ui @testing-library/jest-dom
```

### 2.2 Update [tests/setup.ts](tests/setup.ts)

Delete line 1 (`import '@testing-library/jest-dom'`). Keep the rest (env var seeding). Confirmed safe: `grep toBeInTheDocument|toHaveClass|toHaveTextContent|toBeVisible|toBeDisabled|toHaveAttribute` across [tests/](tests/) returns zero hits — no test uses jest-dom matchers.

### 2.3 Update [package.json](package.json)

Remove the `test:ui` script (line 20) — it references the removed `@vitest/ui`. Keep `test`, `test:watch`, `test:coverage`, `test:e2e`. Playwright stays (user wants E2E capacity for future, even though [tests/e2e/](tests/e2e/) is currently empty).

---

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| [.env.local](.env.local) | Set Supabase URL + anon key (publishable); user fills service role / DB pw / JWT secret |

# Railway Healthcheck Failure — Missing Env Vars

## Context

Commit `a03aed6` shipped to Railway. Build succeeded but healthcheck failed 6/6 times with "service unavailable" — meaning the container never bound to a port. Root cause: [lib/env.ts](lib/env.ts) uses Zod to validate `process.env` and **throws at server boot** if required variables are missing or invalid URLs. On Railway, nothing is injected into `process.env` unless added to the service's Variables panel. The `.env.local` we populated is local-only (gitignored) and never reaches Railway.

Diagnostic evidence:
- [lib/env.ts:64-71](lib/env.ts#L64-L71) — `createEnv()` calls `throw new Error(...)` when `typeof window === 'undefined' && NODE_ENV !== 'test'` — exactly the Railway boot path
- [.next/standalone/server.js:8-9](.next/standalone/server.js#L8-L9) — `server.js` binds to `process.env.PORT || 3000` on `0.0.0.0` → port config is fine
- [supabase/migrations/20260415000001_bootstrap.sql:30](supabase/migrations/20260415000001_bootstrap.sql#L30) — `public._health` table + RLS policy exist → health endpoint would work once service boots
- Railway healthcheck log: "service unavailable" = no socket listening, not an HTTP 503 response → env validation crashed the process before Next could listen

---

## Root Cause

Three env vars are **required to boot**. If any is missing or not a valid URL, Next crashes before binding a port.

| Variable | Validator | Blocks boot? |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` | `z.string().url()` | **YES** |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | `z.string().url()` | **YES** |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | `z.string().min(1)` | **YES** |

Everything else is `.optional()` — the service will boot without them, but specific features will fail when hit (webhooks, emails, AI jobs, etc.).

---

## Action Plan — Variables to Add in Railway

### Service 1 — `web` (add these in the Railway Variables panel for the web service)

#### Required to boot (3)

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://<your-railway-url>.up.railway.app
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=sb_publishable_OORu8axEG5vnGH2VByhO0w_lQK_DR6i
```

> Replace `<your-railway-url>` with whatever Railway shows under the web service → Settings → Networking → Public Networking. If you have a custom domain hooked up, use that instead (e.g. `https://app.inkos.io`).

#### Strongly recommended (server-side features)

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV=production
LOG_LEVEL=info
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<get from https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb/settings/api — "service_role" row, click reveal>
SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET=<same page, "JWT Secret" section>
```

`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is required by:
- Dodo Payments webhook handler (writes subscription rows bypassing RLS)

## Context

Cloud migration + test-dep pruning (Parts 1 & 2 below) already **completed** in prior turn. Remaining work is Part 3: delete three unused CLI scratch directories while keeping `migrations/` and `config.toml` so `pnpm db:migrate` / `pnpm db:types` still work for future schema changes.

---

## Part 1 — Cloud Supabase Migration (DONE)

- ✅ [.env.local](.env.local) swapped: URL + anon (publishable) key + DB password (`Boldnew2026##`) pointing at project `lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb`
- ✅ [supabase/config.toml](supabase/config.toml) `major_version` 15 → 17 (matches cloud Postgres 17)
- ✅ CLI linked: `pnpm dlx supabase link --project-ref lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb`
- ✅ `supabase login` completed (device code `7152f730` authorised)
- ✅ 19 migrations pushed to cloud via `pnpm db:migrate`

# Railway Healthcheck Failure — Missing Env Vars

## Context

Commit `a03aed6` shipped to Railway. Build succeeded but healthcheck failed 6/6 times with "service unavailable" — meaning the container never bound to a port. Root cause: [lib/env.ts](lib/env.ts) uses Zod to validate `process.env` and **throws at server boot** if required variables are missing or invalid URLs. On Railway, nothing is injected into `process.env` unless added to the service's Variables panel. The `.env.local` we populated is local-only (gitignored) and never reaches Railway.

Diagnostic evidence:
- [lib/env.ts:64-71](lib/env.ts#L64-L71) — `createEnv()` calls `throw new Error(...)` when `typeof window === 'undefined' && NODE_ENV !== 'test'` — exactly the Railway boot path
- [.next/standalone/server.js:8-9](.next/standalone/server.js#L8-L9) — `server.js` binds to `process.env.PORT || 3000` on `0.0.0.0` → port config is fine
- [supabase/migrations/20260415000001_bootstrap.sql:30](supabase/migrations/20260415000001_bootstrap.sql#L30) — `public._health` table + RLS policy exist → health endpoint would work once service boots
- Railway healthcheck log: "service unavailable" = no socket listening, not an HTTP 503 response → env validation crashed the process before Next could listen

---

## Root Cause

Three env vars are **required to boot**. If any is missing or not a valid URL, Next crashes before binding a port.

| Variable | Validator | Blocks boot? |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` | `z.string().url()` | **YES** |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | `z.string().url()` | **YES** |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | `z.string().min(1)` | **YES** |

Everything else is `.optional()` — the service will boot without them, but specific features will fail when hit (webhooks, emails, AI jobs, etc.).

---

## Action Plan — Variables to Add in Railway

### Service 1 — `web` (add these in the Railway Variables panel for the web service)

#### Required to boot (3)

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://<your-railway-url>.up.railway.app
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=sb_publishable_OORu8axEG5vnGH2VByhO0w_lQK_DR6i
```

> Replace `<your-railway-url>` with whatever Railway shows under the web service → Settings → Networking → Public Networking. If you have a custom domain hooked up, use that instead (e.g. `https://app.inkos.io`).

#### Strongly recommended (server-side features)

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV=production
LOG_LEVEL=info
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<get from https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb/settings/api — "service_role" row, click reveal>
SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET=<same page, "JWT Secret" section>
```

`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is required by:
- Dodo Payments webhook handler (writes subscription rows bypassing RLS)
- Admin panel (impersonation, GDPR export, studio bans)
- Sprint 8 payroll (writes tax-form rows on behalf of studio)

Without it, the app boots and most of the UI works, but webhooks + admin routes return 500.

#### Payments (needed before first paying customer)

```
DODO_API_KEY=test_... (or live_...)
DODO_PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_KEY=whsec_...
DODO_PRODUCT_SOLO_MONTHLY=
DODO_PRODUCT_SOLO_ANNUAL=
DODO_PRODUCT_STUDIO_MONTHLY=
DODO_PRODUCT_STUDIO_ANNUAL=
DODO_PRODUCT_PRO_MONTHLY=
DODO_PRODUCT_PRO_ANNUAL=
DODO_PRODUCT_ENTERPRISE_MONTHLY=
DODO_PRODUCT_ENTERPRISE_ANNUAL=
DODO_PRODUCT_DEPOSIT=
DODO_PRODUCT_BALANCE_COLLECTION=
```

#### Email (needed for invites, consent-form notifications, booking confirmations)

```
RESEND_API_KEY=re_...
RESEND_FROM_EMAIL=hello@inkos.app
RESEND_REPLY_TO=support@inkos.app
```

#### Observability (optional for launch, high-value post-launch)

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN=https://xxx@sentry.io/xxx
SENTRY_ORG=boldteq
SENTRY_PROJECT=inkos
SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=sntrys_...
NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY=phc_...
NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST=https://app.posthog.com
```

#### Rate limiting (optional but strongly recommended for public routes)

```
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL=https://xxx.upstash.io
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN=xxx
```

Create a free Upstash Redis database at https://console.upstash.com/redis. Without this, [lib/rate-limit.ts](lib/rate-limit.ts) falls back to permit-all mode (public booking endpoint is unprotected).

#### Job queue — needed when Sprint 5/8/9 features are actually used

Provision a Railway Redis plugin (Add Service → Database → Redis), then reference its private URL:

```
REDIS_PRIVATE_URL=${{Redis.REDIS_PRIVATE_URL}}
```

Railway's `${{...}}` syntax auto-injects the private network URL. Required for: AI design generation, payroll PDF rendering, bulk exports, email send workers.

#### AI (Sprint 9 — can defer)

```
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
AI_IMAGE_PROVIDER=openai
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
```

#### TIN encryption (only before accepting W-9 tax info)

```
TIN_ENCRYPTION_KEY=<generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`>
```

Must ALSO be set as a Postgres GUC on the cloud DB: `ALTER DATABASE postgres SET app.settings.tin_encryption_key = '<same value>';` via Dashboard → SQL editor.

---

### Service 2 — `worker-jobs` (separate Railway service)

Workers don't serve HTTP, so they don't need `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` or anon key. They need:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb.supabase.co
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<same as web>
REDIS_PRIVATE_URL=${{Redis.REDIS_PRIVATE_URL}}
LOG_LEVEL=info

# When running AI design jobs:
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...

# When sending emails from background:
RESEND_API_KEY=re_...
RESEND_FROM_EMAIL=hello@inkos.app
```

---

### Service 3 — `worker-cron` (separate Railway service)

Same baseline as worker-jobs:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb.supabase.co
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<same>
REDIS_PRIVATE_URL=${{Redis.REDIS_PRIVATE_URL}}
LOG_LEVEL=info
```

Cron triggers scheduled jobs that are then processed by worker-jobs — it doesn't need Dodo/Resend/AI keys directly.

---

## Minimum to Get Healthcheck Passing

If you just want the web service to come up and pass `/api/health` right now, you only need to add these three to the `web` service:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://<your-railway-url>.up.railway.app
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=sb_publishable_OORu8axEG5vnGH2VByhO0w_lQK_DR6i
```

Then redeploy (Railway will auto-redeploy on variable change, or click "Redeploy"). Healthcheck should pass within 30 seconds. Add the rest incrementally as features come online.

---

## Supabase Dashboard Follow-ups (one-time, manual)

After the web service is up on `https://<your-url>.up.railway.app`, go to https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb/auth/url-configuration and add:

```

---

## Files Modified

None. This is an environment configuration task (all changes happen inside Railway's UI, not in code).

---

## Out of Scope

- Dashboard redirect URL config (flagged above, user will do after deploy)
- Supabase TIN GUC setting (deferred until payroll features are tested)
- Upstash Redis provisioning (recommended but optional)
- Dodo product ID population (needed before first paying customer, not before launch-check)

Pushed `f8ccd92`. Railway should auto-redeploy in ~30 seconds.

## What was happening

Every request path (except `_next/*`, static files, `/api/webhooks`) ran through [proxy.ts](proxy.ts#L14-L58), which:
1. Checks `Host` header against `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`
2. If they don't match → does a DB lookup for a studio with that custom domain
3. If no match → returns **404**

Railway's internal healthcheck hits the container with a **different Host header** than your public URL (internal DNS name, not `inkos-production.up.railway.app`). So `Host ≠ appHost` → 404 every time → healthcheck failure.

## Fix shipped

One-line change to [proxy.ts:70](proxy.ts#L70) — added `api/health` to the matcher's exclusion list. Now `/api/health` bypasses the proxy entirely and the route handler runs directly. It'll return 200 with `{db: "ok"}`.

Fix: force `HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0` in the start script.

Pushed `9c7609b`. Railway will auto-redeploy.

## Why this fixes it

**Before:**
```
Local: http://e9bda3c5d584:8080  ← only listening on container's internal DNS name
```
Railway healthcheck goes through the gateway → the container's network interface has the bind-address `e9bda3c5d584` resolved to a specific IP → healthcheck request arrives on a different interface → connection refused → "service unavailable."

**After:**
```
Local: http://0.0.0.0:8080  ← listening on all interfaces
```
Any incoming connection on port 8080, from any direction, is accepted. Healthcheck reaches `/api/health` → route handler runs → returns 200.

## Watch for in the next Deploy Logs

```
▲ Next.js 16.2.3
- Local:         http://0.0.0.0:8080        ← this line is the signal
- Network:       http://0.0.0.0:8080
✓ Ready in 0ms
```

Then within ~5 seconds:
- ✅ Network › Healthcheck
- Service flips to **Active**
- `https://inkos-production.up.railway.app/api/health` returns `{"status":"healthy",...}`

This is a well-known Railway + Next.js standalone gotcha — not in most docs but catches everyone on their first deploy. Should be the last fix.

# Fix Railway CSS 404 + Delete Local Supabase Folder

## Context

After fixing env vars + proxy matcher + HOSTNAME binding (3 prior commits), Railway deploy finally succeeded — `https://inkos-production.up.railway.app/login` is serving HTML, page title renders as "Sign in | InkOS", all env-gated logic works. **But the page has zero CSS styling** — browser-default fonts, black text on a single purple band (the one inline style that did survive), no Tailwind classes applied, no layout.

Root cause: Next.js `output: 'standalone'` produces a minimal `.next/standalone/` folder that contains the server but **deliberately omits** the `.next/static/` and `public/` folders. The Next.js team expects the deployer to copy those in manually after build. On Railway, `pnpm build` produces the standalone dir but the 6MB of Tailwind CSS + JS bundles in `.next/static/` never reaches the container, so every `/_next/static/*` request 404s.

Verified locally:
- [.next/standalone/](.next/standalone/) contains: `node_modules`, `package.json`, `server.js`, `.next/{BUILD_ID,server,manifests}` — **no `static/`**
- [.next/static/](.next/static/) (at project root) is 6.0 MB — never gets into standalone
- [public/](public/) exists but is empty (0 B) — safe to skip

Separately, user asked to delete the `supabase/` folder now that all 19 migrations are applied to cloud. This is a cleanup step, not a deploy fix.

### A.1 Add `postbuild` script to [package.json](package.json)

Immediately after the existing `build` script, add a step that copies both folders into `.next/standalone/` so Railway's `node .next/standalone/server.js` can serve them:

```json
"build": "next build",
"postbuild": "cp -r public .next/standalone/ && cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/",
```

`pnpm` runs `postbuild` automatically after `build` — no change to Railway's `buildCommand` needed.

Notes on the command:
- `cp -r public .next/standalone/` works even when public/ is empty (creates the dir inside standalone).
- `cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/` copies the 6 MB of hashed assets to where `server.js` expects them.
- Using POSIX `cp` — works on Railway's Linux containers. Local Mac builds also work (macOS ships BSD cp which behaves the same for these flags).

### A.2 Verify locally

```

ls .next/standalone/.next/static    # should now list chunks/, css/, media/

# Railway Healthcheck Failure — Missing Env Vars

## Context

Commit `a03aed6` shipped to Railway. Build succeeded but healthcheck failed 6/6 times with "service unavailable" — meaning the container never bound to a port. Root cause: [lib/env.ts](lib/env.ts) uses Zod to validate `process.env` and **throws at server boot** if required variables are missing or invalid URLs. On Railway, nothing is injected into `process.env` unless added to the service's Variables panel. The `.env.local` we populated is local-only (gitignored) and never reaches Railway.

Diagnostic evidence:
- [lib/env.ts:64-71](lib/env.ts#L64-L71) — `createEnv()` calls `throw new Error(...)` when `typeof window === 'undefined' && NODE_ENV !== 'test'` — exactly the Railway boot path
- [.next/standalone/server.js:8-9](.next/standalone/server.js#L8-L9) — `server.js` binds to `process.env.PORT || 3000` on `0.0.0.0` → port config is fine
- [supabase/migrations/20260415000001_bootstrap.sql:30](supabase/migrations/20260415000001_bootstrap.sql#L30) — `public._health` table + RLS policy exist → health endpoint would work once service boots
- Railway healthcheck log: "service unavailable" = no socket listening, not an HTTP 503 response → env validation crashed the process before Next could listen

---

## Root Cause

Three env vars are **required to boot**. If any is missing or not a valid URL, Next crashes before binding a port.

| Variable | Validator | Blocks boot? |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` | `z.string().url()` | **YES** |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | `z.string().url()` | **YES** |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | `z.string().min(1)` | **YES** |

Everything else is `.optional()` — the service will boot without them, but specific features will fail when hit (webhooks, emails, AI jobs, etc.).

---

## Action Plan — Variables to Add in Railway

### Service 1 — `web` (add these in the Railway Variables panel for the web service)

#### Required to boot (3)

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://<your-railway-url>.up.railway.app
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=sb_publishable_OORu8axEG5vnGH2VByhO0w_lQK_DR6i
```

> Replace `<your-railway-url>` with whatever Railway shows under the web service → Settings → Networking → Public Networking. If you have a custom domain hooked up, use that instead (e.g. `https://app.inkos.io`).

#### Strongly recommended (server-side features)

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV=production
LOG_LEVEL=info
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<get from https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb/settings/api — "service_role" row, click reveal>
SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET=<same page, "JWT Secret" section>
```

`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is required by:
- Dodo Payments webhook handler (writes subscription rows bypassing RLS)
- Admin panel (impersonation, GDPR export, studio bans)
- Sprint 8 payroll (writes tax-form rows on behalf of studio)

Without it, the app boots and most of the UI works, but webhooks + admin routes return 500.

#### Payments (needed before first paying customer)

```
DODO_API_KEY=test_... (or live_...)
DODO_PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_KEY=whsec_...
DODO_PRODUCT_SOLO_MONTHLY=
DODO_PRODUCT_SOLO_ANNUAL=
DODO_PRODUCT_STUDIO_MONTHLY=
DODO_PRODUCT_STUDIO_ANNUAL=
DODO_PRODUCT_PRO_MONTHLY=
DODO_PRODUCT_PRO_ANNUAL=
DODO_PRODUCT_ENTERPRISE_MONTHLY=
DODO_PRODUCT_ENTERPRISE_ANNUAL=
DODO_PRODUCT_DEPOSIT=
DODO_PRODUCT_BALANCE_COLLECTION=
```

#### Email (needed for invites, consent-form notifications, booking confirmations)

```
RESEND_API_KEY=re_...
RESEND_FROM_EMAIL=hello@inkos.app
RESEND_REPLY_TO=support@inkos.app
```

#### Observability (optional for launch, high-value post-launch)

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN=https://xxx@sentry.io/xxx
SENTRY_ORG=boldteq
SENTRY_PROJECT=inkos
SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=sntrys_...
NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY=phc_...
NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST=https://app.posthog.com
```

#### Rate limiting (optional but strongly recommended for public routes)

```
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL=https://xxx.upstash.io
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN=xxx
```

Create a free Upstash Redis database at https://console.upstash.com/redis. Without this, [lib/rate-limit.ts](lib/rate-limit.ts) falls back to permit-all mode (public booking endpoint is unprotected).

#### Job queue — needed when Sprint 5/8/9 features are actually used

Provision a Railway Redis plugin (Add Service → Database → Redis), then reference its private URL:

```
REDIS_PRIVATE_URL=${{Redis.REDIS_PRIVATE_URL}}
```

Railway's `${{...}}` syntax auto-injects the private network URL. Required for: AI design generation, payroll PDF rendering, bulk exports, email send workers.

#### AI (Sprint 9 — can defer)

```
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
AI_IMAGE_PROVIDER=openai
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
```

#### TIN encryption (only before accepting W-9 tax info)

```
TIN_ENCRYPTION_KEY=<generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`>
```

Must ALSO be set as a Postgres GUC on the cloud DB: `ALTER DATABASE postgres SET app.settings.tin_encryption_key = '<same value>';` via Dashboard → SQL editor.

---

### Service 2 — `worker-jobs` (separate Railway service)

Workers don't serve HTTP, so they don't need `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` or anon key. They need:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb.supabase.co
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<same as web>
REDIS_PRIVATE_URL=${{Redis.REDIS_PRIVATE_URL}}
LOG_LEVEL=info

# When running AI design jobs:
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...

# When sending emails from background:
RESEND_API_KEY=re_...
RESEND_FROM_EMAIL=hello@inkos.app
```

---

### Service 3 — `worker-cron` (separate Railway service)

Same baseline as worker-jobs:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb.supabase.co
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<same>
REDIS_PRIVATE_URL=${{Redis.REDIS_PRIVATE_URL}}
LOG_LEVEL=info
```

Cron triggers scheduled jobs that are then processed by worker-jobs — it doesn't need Dodo/Resend/AI keys directly.

---

## Minimum to Get Healthcheck Passing

If you just want the web service to come up and pass `/api/health` right now, you only need to add these three to the `web` service:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://<your-railway-url>.up.railway.app
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=sb_publishable_OORu8axEG5vnGH2VByhO0w_lQK_DR6i
```

Then redeploy (Railway will auto-redeploy on variable change, or click "Redeploy"). Healthcheck should pass within 30 seconds. Add the rest incrementally as features come online.

---

## Supabase Dashboard Follow-ups (one-time, manual)

After the web service is up on `https://<your-url>.up.railway.app`, go to https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb/auth/url-configuration and add:

```
Site URL: https://<your-railway-url>.up.railway.app
Redirect URLs: https://<your-railway-url>.up.railway.app/**
```

Without this, Supabase Auth's magic-link / OAuth redirects bounce back to localhost:3100.

---

## Verification

1. Add the 3 required vars to the `web` service in Railway
2. Wait for auto-redeploy (or click Redeploy manually)
3. Watch deploy logs → should see `Ready on http://0.0.0.0:<port>` within 10 seconds
4. Railway healthcheck retries `/api/health` → should return `{"status":"healthy","checks":{"web":"ok","db":"ok"}}` and flip the service to Active
5. `curl https://<your-railway-url>.up.railway.app/api/health` from your laptop → same response
6. Open the URL in browser → should redirect to `/login`
7. If healthcheck still fails: check deploy logs for the actual error — look for `[InkOS] Invalid environment variables:` which means Zod validation failed and will tell you which var is wrong

---

## Files Modified

None. This is an environment configuration task (all changes happen inside Railway's UI, not in code).

---

## Out of Scope

- Dashboard redirect URL config (flagged above, user will do after deploy)
- Supabase TIN GUC setting (deferred until payroll features are tested)
- Upstash Redis provisioning (recommended but optional)
- Dodo product ID population (needed before first paying customer, not before launch-check)

# Fix Railway CSS 404 + Delete Local Supabase Folder

## Context

After fixing env vars + proxy matcher + HOSTNAME binding (3 prior commits), Railway deploy finally succeeded — `https://inkos-production.up.railway.app/login` is serving HTML, page title renders as "Sign in | InkOS", all env-gated logic works. **But the page has zero CSS styling** — browser-default fonts, black text on a single purple band (the one inline style that did survive), no Tailwind classes applied, no layout.

Root cause: Next.js `output: 'standalone'` produces a minimal `.next/standalone/` folder that contains the server but **deliberately omits** the `.next/static/` and `public/` folders. The Next.js team expects the deployer to copy those in manually after build. On Railway, `pnpm build` produces the standalone dir but the 6MB of Tailwind CSS + JS bundles in `.next/static/` never reaches the container, so every `/_next/static/*` request 404s.

Verified locally:
- [.next/standalone/](.next/standalone/) contains: `node_modules`, `package.json`, `server.js`, `.next/{BUILD_ID,server,manifests}` — **no `static/`**
- [.next/static/](.next/static/) (at project root) is 6.0 MB — never gets into standalone
- [public/](public/) exists but is empty (0 B) — safe to skip

Separately, user asked to delete the `supabase/` folder now that all 19 migrations are applied to cloud. This is a cleanup step, not a deploy fix.

---

## Part A — Fix CSS 404 on Railway (blocking, urgent)

### A.1 Add `postbuild` script to [package.json](package.json)

Immediately after the existing `build` script, add a step that copies both folders into `.next/standalone/` so Railway's `node .next/standalone/server.js` can serve them:

```json
"build": "next build",
"postbuild": "cp -r public .next/standalone/ && cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/",
```

`pnpm` runs `postbuild` automatically after `build` — no change to Railway's `buildCommand` needed.

Notes on the command:
- `cp -r public .next/standalone/` works even when public/ is empty (creates the dir inside standalone).
- `cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/` copies the 6 MB of hashed assets to where `server.js` expects them.
- Using POSIX `cp` — works on Railway's Linux containers. Local Mac builds also work (macOS ships BSD cp which behaves the same for these flags).

### A.2 Verify locally

```
rm -rf .next && pnpm build
ls .next/standalone/.next/static    # should now list chunks/, css/, media/
ls .next/standalone/public          # should exist (empty is fine)
```

### A.3 No other code changes

[next.config.ts](next.config.ts) already has `output: 'standalone'` + `outputFileTracingRoot: __dirname` (we fixed this earlier). Start script [package.json:start](package.json) already has `HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0 node .next/standalone/server.js`. [railway.toml](railway.toml) runs `pnpm start` which will pick everything up.

---

## Part B — Delete Local `supabase/` Folder

Now that all migrations are in cloud and verified applied, remove the local CLI tooling surface. User explicitly opted into the full delete this time (previous plan kept it — this overrides).

### B.1 Delete the folder

```
rm -rf supabase/
```

This removes:
- `supabase/migrations/` (19 committed migrations — schema history stays in git log forever, can be restored with `git checkout HEAD~ -- supabase/migrations` if ever needed)
- `supabase/config.toml`

### B.2 Remove now-broken scripts from [package.json](package.json)

These three scripts reference the deleted folder and will throw if run:

```
"db:migrate": "supabase db push",
"db:types": "supabase gen types typescript --linked > lib/supabase/types.ts",
"db:reset": "supabase db reset",
```

Delete all three. Future schema edits will happen in the Supabase Dashboard SQL editor.

### B.3 Remove unused `supabase` CLI devDep

Without the folder + scripts, the CLI has no use. Remove from [package.json](package.json) devDependencies:

```
"supabase": "2.22.6",
```

Run `pnpm install --prefer-offline --ignore-scripts` to sync lockfile.

### B.4 Optionally clean `.gitignore`

These lines reference paths that no longer exist:

```
.supabase/
supabase/.temp/
supabase/.branches/
```

Can be removed, but harmless if left. Skip unless it bothers you — keep the plan tight.

---

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [package.json](package.json) | Add `postbuild` script; remove `db:migrate`/`db:types`/`db:reset` scripts; remove `supabase` devDep |
| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | Auto-updated by `pnpm install` |
| `supabase/` (deleted) | Entire folder removed on disk (history preserved in git) |

---

## Verification

### For Part A (CSS fix)

1. `rm -rf .next && pnpm build` → build succeeds, `postbuild` runs silently
2. `ls .next/standalone/.next/static/css/` → lists one or more `.css` files
3. `ls .next/standalone/.next/static/chunks/` → lists JS chunks
4. Commit + push → Railway auto-redeploys (~3 min)
5. Visit `https://inkos-production.up.railway.app/login` → page renders with full Tailwind styling, InkOS brand colors, shadcn components
6. Open DevTools → Network tab → filter by `_next/static` → every request returns 200 (not 404)

### For Part B (folder delete)

1. `ls supabase/` → "No such file or directory"
2. `pnpm typecheck` → still passes (no app code imports from `supabase/`)
3. `pnpm test` → 46/46 pass
4. `pnpm build` → still succeeds
5. Future schema changes: log into https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb/sql/new and run SQL directly

---

## Out of Scope

- Re-linking CLI later: if user ever wants `pnpm db:migrate` back, run `pnpm add -D supabase && pnpm dlx supabase init && pnpm dlx supabase link --project-ref lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb && pnpm dlx supabase db pull` to regenerate migrations from cloud.
- Supabase Dashboard redirect URL config (flagged in prior plan — user will do manually).
- Fixing inventory/payroll schema drift (separate sprint).
- Worker service deploys (worker-jobs, worker-cron) — these are separate Railway services, same CSS fix won't apply to them (they're not HTTP servers). Deploy them after web service is confirmed healthy.

toolUseResult.plan:
# Fix Railway CSS 404 + Delete Local Supabase Folder

## Context

After fixing env vars + proxy matcher + HOSTNAME binding (3 prior commits), Railway deploy finally succeeded — `https://inkos-production.up.railway.app/login` is serving HTML, page title renders as "Sign in | InkOS", all env-gated logic works. **But the page has zero CSS styling** — browser-default fonts, black text on a single purple band (the one inline style that did survive), no Tailwind classes applied, no layout.

Root cause: Next.js `output: 'standalone'` produces a minimal `.next/standalone/` folder that contains the server but **deliberately omits** the `.next/static/` and `public/` folders. The Next.js team expects the deployer to copy those in manually after build. On Railway, `pnpm build` produces the standalone dir but the 6MB of Tailwind CSS + JS bundles in `.next/static/` never reaches the container, so every `/_next/static/*` request 404s.

Verified locally:
- [.next/standalone/](.next/standalone/) contains: `node_modules`, `package.json`, `server.js`, `.next/{BUILD_ID,server,manifests}` — **no `static/`**
- [.next/static/](.next/static/) (at project root) is 6.0 MB — never gets into standalone
- [public/](public/) exists but is empty (0 B) — safe to skip

Separately, user asked to delete the `supabase/` folder now that all 19 migrations are applied to cloud. This is a cleanup step, not a deploy fix.

---

## Part A — Fix CSS 404 on Railway (blocking, urgent)

### A.1 Add `postbuild` script to [package.json](package.json)

Immediately after the existing `build` script, add a step that copies both folders into `.next/standalone/` so Railway's `node .next/standalone/server.js` can serve them:

```json
"build": "next build",
"postbuild": "cp -r public .next/standalone/ && cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/",
```

`pnpm` runs `postbuild` automatically after `build` — no change to Railway's `buildCommand` needed.

Notes on the command:
- `cp -r public .next/standalone/` works even when public/ is empty (creates the dir inside standalone).
- `cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/` copies the 6 MB of hashed assets to where `server.js` expects them.
- Using POSIX `cp` — works on Railway's Linux containers. Local Mac builds also work (macOS ships BSD cp which behaves the same for these flags).

### A.2 Verify locally

```
rm -rf .next && pnpm build
ls .next/standalone/.next/static    # should now list chunks/, css/, media/
ls .next/standalone/public          # should exist (empty is fine)
```

### A.3 No other code changes

[next.config.ts](next.config.ts) already has `output: 'standalone'` + `outputFileTracingRoot: __dirname` (we fixed this earlier). Start script [package.json:start](package.json) already has `HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0 node .next/standalone/server.js`. [railway.toml](railway.toml) runs `pnpm start` which will pick everything up.

---

## Part B — Delete Local `supabase/` Folder

Now that all migrations are in cloud and verified applied, remove the local CLI tooling surface. User explicitly opted into the full delete this time (previous plan kept it — this overrides).

### B.1 Delete the folder

```
rm -rf supabase/
```

This removes:
- `supabase/migrations/` (19 committed migrations — schema history stays in git log forever, can be restored with `git checkout HEAD~ -- supabase/migrations` if ever needed)
- `supabase/config.toml`

### B.2 Remove now-broken scripts from [package.json](package.json)

These three scripts reference the deleted folder and will throw if run:

```
"db:migrate": "supabase db push",
"db:types": "supabase gen types typescript --linked > lib/supabase/types.ts",
"db:reset": "supabase db reset",
```

Delete all three. Future schema edits will happen in the Supabase Dashboard SQL editor.

### B.3 Remove unused `supabase` CLI devDep

Without the folder + scripts, the CLI has no use. Remove from [package.json](package.json) devDependencies:

```
"supabase": "2.22.6",
```

Run `pnpm install --prefer-offline --ignore-scripts` to sync lockfile.

### B.4 Optionally clean `.gitignore`

These lines reference paths that no longer exist:

```
.supabase/
supabase/.temp/
supabase/.branches/
```

Can be removed, but harmless if left. Skip unless it bothers you — keep the plan tight.

---

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [package.json](package.json) | Add `postbuild` script; remove `db:migrate`/`db:types`/`db:reset` scripts; remove `supabase` devDep |
| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | Auto-updated by `pnpm install` |
| `supabase/` (deleted) | Entire folder removed on disk (history preserved in git) |

---

## Verification

### For Part A (CSS fix)

1. `rm -rf .next && pnpm build` → build succeeds, `postbuild` runs silently
2. `ls .next/standalone/.next/static/css/` → lists one or more `.css` files
3. `ls .next/standalone/.next/static/chunks/` → lists JS chunks
4. Commit + push → Railway auto-redeploys (~3 min)
5. Visit `https://inkos-production.up.railway.app/login` → page renders with full Tailwind styling, InkOS brand colors, shadcn components
6. Open DevTools → Network tab → filter by `_next/static` → every request returns 200 (not 404)

### For Part B (folder delete)

1. `ls supabase/` → "No such file or directory"
2. `pnpm typecheck` → still passes (no app code imports from `supabase/`)
3. `pnpm test` → 46/46 pass
4. `pnpm build` → still succeeds
5. Future schema changes: log into https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb/sql/new and run SQL directly

---

## Out of Scope

- Re-linking CLI later: if user ever wants `pnpm db:migrate` back, run `pnpm add -D supabase && pnpm dlx supabase init && pnpm dlx supabase link --project-ref lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb && pnpm dlx supabase db pull` to regenerate migrations from cloud.
- Supabase Dashboard redirect URL config (flagged in prior plan — user will do manually).
- Fixing inventory/payroll schema drift (separate sprint).
- Worker service deploys (worker-jobs, worker-cron) — these are separate Railway services, same CSS fix won't apply to them (they're not HTTP servers). Deploy them after web service is confirmed healthy.

# Fix Railway CSS 404 + Delete Local Supabase Folder

## Context

After fixing env vars + proxy matcher + HOSTNAME binding (3 prior commits), Railway deploy finally succeeded — `https://inkos-production.up.railway.app/login` is serving HTML, page title renders as "Sign in | InkOS", all env-gated logic works. **But the page has zero CSS styling** — browser-default fonts, black text on a single purple band (the one inline style that did survive), no Tailwind classes applied, no layout.

Root cause: Next.js `output: 'standalone'` produces a minimal `.next/standalone/` folder that contains the server but **deliberately omits** the `.next/static/` and `public/` folders. The Next.js team expects the deployer to copy those in manually after build. On Railway, `pnpm build` produces the standalone dir but the 6MB of Tailwind CSS + JS bundles in `.next/static/` never reaches the container, so every `/_next/static/*` request 404s.

Verified locally:
- [.next/standalone/](.next/standalone/) contains: `node_modules`, `package.json`, `server.js`, `.next/{BUILD_ID,server,manifests}` — **no `static/`**
- [.next/static/](.next/static/) (at project root) is 6.0 MB — never gets into standalone
- [public/](public/) exists but is empty (0 B) — safe to skip

Separately, user asked to delete the `supabase/` folder now that all 19 migrations are applied to cloud. This is a cleanup step, not a deploy fix.

---

## Part A — Fix CSS 404 on Railway (blocking, urgent)

### A.1 Add `postbuild` script to [package.json](package.json)

Immediately after the existing `build` script, add a step that copies both folders into `.next/standalone/` so Railway's `node .next/standalone/server.js` can serve them:

```json
"build": "next build",
"postbuild": "cp -r public .next/standalone/ && cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/",
```

`pnpm` runs `postbuild` automatically after `build` — no change to Railway's `buildCommand` needed.

Notes on the command:
- `cp -r public .next/standalone/` works even when public/ is empty (creates the dir inside standalone).
- `cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/` copies the 6 MB of hashed assets to where `server.js` expects them.
- Using POSIX `cp` — works on Railway's Linux containers. Local Mac builds also work (macOS ships BSD cp which behaves the same for these flags).

### A.2 Verify locally

```
rm -rf .next && pnpm build
ls .next/standalone/.next/static    # should now list chunks/, css/, media/
ls .next/standalone/public          # should exist (empty is fine)
```

### A.3 No other code changes

[next.config.ts](next.config.ts) already has `output: 'standalone'` + `outputFileTracingRoot: __dirname` (we fixed this earlier). Start script [package.json:start](package.json) already has `HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0 node .next/standalone/server.js`. [railway.toml](railway.toml) runs `pnpm start` which will pick everything up.

---

## Part B — Delete Local `supabase/` Folder

Now that all migrations are in cloud and verified applied, remove the local CLI tooling surface. User explicitly opted into the full delete this time (previous plan kept it — this overrides).

### B.1 Delete the folder

```
rm -rf supabase/
```

This removes:
- `supabase/migrations/` (19 committed migrations — schema history stays in git log forever, can be restored with `git checkout HEAD~ -- supabase/migrations` if ever needed)
- `supabase/config.toml`

### B.2 Remove now-broken scripts from [package.json](package.json)

These three scripts reference the deleted folder and will throw if run:

```
"db:migrate": "supabase db push",
"db:types": "supabase gen types typescript --linked > lib/supabase/types.ts",
"db:reset": "supabase db reset",
```

Delete all three. Future schema edits will happen in the Supabase Dashboard SQL editor.

### B.3 Remove unused `supabase` CLI devDep

Without the folder + scripts, the CLI has no use. Remove from [package.json](package.json) devDependencies:

```
"supabase": "2.22.6",
```

Run `pnpm install --prefer-offline --ignore-scripts` to sync lockfile.

### B.4 Optionally clean `.gitignore`

These lines reference paths that no longer exist:

```
.supabase/
supabase/.temp/
supabase/.branches/
```

Can be removed, but harmless if left. Skip unless it bothers you — keep the plan tight.

---

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [package.json](package.json) | Add `postbuild` script; remove `db:migrate`/`db:types`/`db:reset` scripts; remove `supabase` devDep |
| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | Auto-updated by `pnpm install` |
| `supabase/` (deleted) | Entire folder removed on disk (history preserved in git) |

---

## Verification

### For Part A (CSS fix)

1. `rm -rf .next && pnpm build` → build succeeds, `postbuild` runs silently
2. `ls .next/standalone/.next/static/css/` → lists one or more `.css` files
3. `ls .next/standalone/.next/static/chunks/` → lists JS chunks
4. Commit + push → Railway auto-redeploys (~3 min)
5. Visit `https://inkos-production.up.railway.app/login` → page renders with full Tailwind styling, InkOS brand colors, shadcn components
6. Open DevTools → Network tab → filter by `_next/static` → every request returns 200 (not 404)

### For Part B (folder delete)

1. `ls supabase/` → "No such file or directory"
2. `pnpm typecheck` → still passes (no app code imports from `supabase/`)
3. `pnpm test` → 46/46 pass
4. `pnpm build` → still succeeds
5. Future schema changes: log into https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb/sql/new and run SQL directly

---

## Out of Scope

- Re-linking CLI later: if user ever wants `pnpm db:migrate` back, run `pnpm add -D supabase && pnpm dlx supabase init && pnpm dlx supabase link --project-ref lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb && pnpm dlx supabase db pull` to regenerate migrations from cloud.
- Supabase Dashboard redirect URL config (flagged in prior plan — user will do manually).
- Fixing inventory/payroll schema drift (separate sprint).
- Worker service deploys (worker-jobs, worker-cron) — these are separate Railway services, same CSS fix won't apply to them (they're not HTTP servers). Deploy them after web service is confirmed healthy.

# Fix Railway CSS 404 + Delete Local Supabase Folder

## Context

After fixing env vars + proxy matcher + HOSTNAME binding (3 prior commits), Railway deploy finally succeeded — `https://inkos-production.up.railway.app/login` is serving HTML, page title renders as "Sign in | InkOS", all env-gated logic works. **But the page has zero CSS styling** — browser-default fonts, black text on a single purple band (the one inline style that did survive), no Tailwind classes applied, no layout.

Root cause: Next.js `output: 'standalone'` produces a minimal `.next/standalone/` folder that contains the server but **deliberately omits** the `.next/static/` and `public/` folders. The Next.js team expects the deployer to copy those in manually after build. On Railway, `pnpm build` produces the standalone dir but the 6MB of Tailwind CSS + JS bundles in `.next/static/` never reaches the container, so every `/_next/static/*` request 404s.

Verified locally:
- [.next/standalone/](.next/standalone/) contains: `node_modules`, `package.json`, `server.js`, `.next/{BUILD_ID,server,manifests}` — **no `static/`**
- [.next/static/](.next/static/) (at project root) is 6.0 MB — never gets into standalone
- [public/](public/) exists but is empty (0 B) — safe to skip

Separately, user asked to delete the `supabase/` folder now that all 19 migrations are applied to cloud. This is a cleanup step, not a deploy fix.

---

## Part A — Fix CSS 404 on Railway (blocking, urgent)

### A.1 Add `postbuild` script to [package.json](package.json)

```json
"build": "next build",
"postbuild": "cp -r public .next/standalone/ && cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/",
```

`pnpm` runs `postbuild` automatically after `build` — no change to Railway's `buildCommand` needed.

Notes on the command:
- `cp -r public .next/standalone/` works even when public/ is empty (creates the dir inside standalone).
- `cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/` copies the 6 MB of hashed assets to where `server.js` expects them.
- Using POSIX `cp` — works on Railway's Linux containers. Local Mac builds also work (macOS ships BSD cp which behaves the same for these flags).

### A.2 Verify locally

```
rm -rf .next && pnpm build
ls .next/standalone/.next/static    # should now list chunks/, css/, media/
ls .next/standalone/public          # should exist (empty is fine)
```

### A.3 No other code changes

[next.config.ts](next.config.ts) already has `output: 'standalone'` + `outputFileTracingRoot: __dirname` (we fixed this earlier). Start script [package.json:start](package.json) already has `HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0 node .next/standalone/server.js`. [railway.toml](railway.toml) runs `pnpm start` which will pick everything up.

content.text:
Pushed `6f7cd19`. The fix:

- `railway.toml` `buildCommand` was bleeding into worker Dockerfiles (Railway bug — it overrides all services in the repo)
- Moved `cp` commands **inside** `package.json`'s `build` script — workers use their own Dockerfiles which call `pnpm --filter @inkos/worker-jobs run build`, not the root `build` script, so they're unaffected
- `railway.toml` now just runs `pnpm install && pnpm build` which triggers the full copy automatically

Railway will now rebuild cleanly. Wait ~4 min and check the login page.

4
RUN  pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build
135ms
/bin/bash: line 1: pnpm: command not found
Dockerfile:15
-------------------
13 |     # build phase
14 |     COPY . /app/.
15 | >>> RUN  pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build
16 |
17 |
-------------------
ERROR: failed to build: failed to solve: process "/bin/bash -ol pipefail -c pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build" did not complete successfully: exit code: 127
Error: Docker build failed

Railway is still injecting `buildCommand` into the worker Dockerfiles. The `[build] buildCommand` in `railway.toml` applies to ALL services in the project, including Docker-based ones. The only fix is to remove `buildCommand` from `railway.toml` entirely — the workers don't need it, and the web service will fall back to Nixpacks auto-detection which runs `pnpm install && pnpm build` anyway.

### BUG 2: deploy.yml is incomplete
- **Status:** Deployment steps are commented out with `# TODO (Bolt): Configure Railway deployment`
- **Impact:** CI passes but deploy doesn't run
- **Fix:** Uncomment and add Railway CLI commands for each service

### BUG 3: health endpoint missing detailed checks
- **Status:** `/api/health/route.ts` exists but likely minimal
- **Fix:** Ensure it checks:
  - DB connectivity (Supabase query)
  - Redis connectivity (if workers enabled)
  - Return 503 if any check fails

### BUG 4: redis_private_url without Redis crashes at runtime
- **Status:** `lib/queue.ts` throws if REDIS_PRIVATE_URL missing
- **Impact:** Any enqueueJob() call = app crash in production
- **Fix:** Either keep Redis + workers, or refactor queue calls

### BUG 5: build script copies public files manually
- **Status:** `"build": "next build && cp -r public .next/standalone/ && cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/"`
- **Impact:** Works, but fragile
- **Fix:** Railway should handle this with proper Dockerfile

### BUG 6: No .dockerignore
- **Status:** Rankora has one, InkOS doesn't
- **Impact:** Docker build includes unnecessary files (tests, scripts, node_modules)
- **Fix:** Create `.dockerignore` based on Rankora's

- **Status:** If set but auth token missing, source maps won't upload
- **Impact:** Sentry errors show minified code
- **Fix:** Ensure `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` is set in Railway for CI builds

- **Status:** No `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY` in .env.local
- **Impact:** Analytics not running

Remove test/dev-only deps. Keep workers and queue.

.next

vitest.config.ts
.env.local

- name: Deploy worker-jobs

- name: Deploy worker-cron

  env:

```

### Step 6: Set Railway env vars
Copy `.env.example` → Railway variables, fill in secrets.

### Step 7: Deploy to Railway
```bash
railway up
```

---

|----------|--------|--------|
| **Workers** | Coupled to app | Keep + Deploy 3 services |
| **Tests** | Optional | Remove for MVP |
| **Scripts** | Dev-only | Remove vega-review |

1. Managed Redis (Railway plugin)
2. 3 Railway services (web, worker-jobs, worker-cron)

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
# Multi-stage Dockerfile for Rankora (Next.js 16 App Router) on Railway.
#
# Uses Next.js standalone output (enabled in next.config.ts) so the
# final image only contains the compiled server + required node_modules,
# producing a ~150MB image instead of ~1GB.
#
# Layers are ordered for maximum cache reuse:
#   1. deps    — installs npm packages (cached unless package*.json changes)
#   2. builder — runs `next build` (cached unless source changes)
#   3. runner  — slim runtime layer with only what's needed to serve

# ─── 1. deps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS deps
# libc6-compat is required by some native npm packages (sharp, etc.)
RUN apk add --no-cache libc6-compat
WORKDIR /app

# Copy only manifest + lockfile for maximum layer-cache reuse
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
# --legacy-peer-deps mirrors how we install locally (React 19 peer
# conflicts with some older Radix/vaul deps; safe to override)
RUN npm ci --legacy-peer-deps

# ─── 2. builder ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .

# Next.js telemetry off — Railway build logs stay clean
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1

# Build-time env vars that MUST be baked into the client bundle.
# Railway injects these via Dockerfile ARG → ENV bridge. Set the same
# variable in Railway's Variables tab and Railway will expose it as a
# build arg automatically.
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN
ARG SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN
ARG SENTRY_ORG
ARG SENTRY_PROJECT

ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN \
    SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=$SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN \
    SENTRY_ORG=$SENTRY_ORG \
    SENTRY_PROJECT=$SENTRY_PROJECT

RUN npm run build

# ─── 3. runner ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app

ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \
    PORT=8080 \
    HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0

# Run as non-root. Railway does this automatically but we double down.
RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs && \
    adduser --system --uid 1001 nextjs

# Copy only what's needed to run the server
COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static

USER nextjs
EXPOSE 8080

# Standalone output includes a `server.js` entry point at the repo root
CMD ["node", "server.js"]

# InkOS Minimal Strip — Next.js + Supabase + Railway

## Context

Railway deploy has failed multiple times. Root cause: the repo has 3 services (web + 2 workers), workspace packages, Redis dependency, and a bleeding `railway.toml` that injects its `buildCommand` into worker Dockerfiles. User deleted the Railway project and wants to START OVER with the simplest possible setup:

**Goal: one service. Next.js app → Supabase → Railway. Nothing else.**

Workers, BullMQ, Redis, node-cron, workspaces, testing infra — all out for now. Can add back later feature by feature when actually needed.

Model the setup on **Rankora** (working Stack A reference): single Next.js app, Dockerfile (not Nixpacks), standalone output, Supabase cloud. No workers, no workspace, no Redis.

---

## Current Problems (discovered in audit)

1. **`railway.toml` `buildCommand` bleeds into worker Dockerfiles** — the root cause of every failed Docker build. Railway injects the global build command into Docker-based services too.
2. **Workspace package (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`)** references 2 worker dirs that don't need to deploy.
3. **`lib/queue.ts`** is imported by 11 API routes — all non-critical (email sends, PDF generation, AI design, marketing). **None block auth/login/signup/dashboard.** Queue only fails when those specific routes are hit, not at boot.
4. **Nixpacks builder is fragile** — doesn't reliably run `postbuild` hook; doesn't cleanly handle our `cp` commands.
5. **Too many moving parts** — tests, scripts/vega-review, husky, lint-staged, sentry, upstash, pino-pretty etc. Each is one more thing that can break the build.

---

## The Strip — What Stays, What Goes

# InkOS Minimal Strip — Next.js + Supabase + Railway

## Context

Railway deploy has failed multiple times. Root cause: the repo has 3 services (web + 2 workers), workspace packages, Redis dependency, and a bleeding `railway.toml` that injects its `buildCommand` into worker Dockerfiles. User deleted the Railway project and wants to START OVER with the simplest possible setup:

**Goal: one service. Next.js app → Supabase → Railway. Nothing else.**

Workers, BullMQ, Redis, node-cron, workspaces, testing infra — all out for now. Can add back later feature by feature when actually needed.

Model the setup on **Rankora** (working Stack A reference): single Next.js app, Dockerfile (not Nixpacks), standalone output, Supabase cloud. No workers, no workspace, no Redis.

---

## Current Problems (discovered in audit)

1. **`railway.toml` `buildCommand` bleeds into worker Dockerfiles** — the root cause of every failed Docker build. Railway injects the global build command into Docker-based services too.
2. **Workspace package (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`)** references 2 worker dirs that don't need to deploy.
3. **`lib/queue.ts`** is imported by 11 API routes — all non-critical (email sends, PDF generation, AI design, marketing). **None block auth/login/signup/dashboard.** Queue only fails when those specific routes are hit, not at boot.
4. **Nixpacks builder is fragile** — doesn't reliably run `postbuild` hook; doesn't cleanly handle our `cp` commands.
5. **Too many moving parts** — tests, scripts/vega-review, husky, lint-staged, sentry, upstash, pino-pretty etc. Each is one more thing that can break the build.

---

## The Strip — What Stays, What Goes

### KEEP (minimum viable Next + Supabase)
```
app/                         Next.js routes
components/                  React UI
hooks/                       React hooks
lib/                         utilities (supabase, env, logger, utils)

.env.local                   local only, git-ignored

postcss.config.mjs

next-env.d.ts

```

### DELETE (out of scope for minimum viable)

workers/                     entire folder (jobs + cron Dockerfiles)
tests/                       all test files
scripts/                     vega-review.ts
.husky/                      git hooks
.github/                     CI workflows (optional; Railway auto-deploys on push)
sentry.client.config.ts
sentry.edge.config.ts
sentry.server.config.ts
instrumentation.ts           Sentry-only (no other use)
instrumentation-client.ts    Sentry-only
vitest.config.ts
eslint.config.mjs            keep for local dev, not needed for deploy
.prettierrc
DEPLOY.md, ROLLBACK.md, PORTS.md
pnpm-workspace.yaml          no more workspaces
```

### REFACTOR (remove the code that depends on deleted deps)

**Queue removal** — replace every `enqueueJob('X', ...)` call with a TODO stub that logs + returns. No functionality change for login/signup/dashboard. Feature routes (email, PDF, AI, marketing) degrade gracefully.

# InkOS Minimal Strip — Next.js + Supabase + Railway

## Context

Railway deploy has failed multiple times. Root cause: the repo has 3 services (web + 2 workers), workspace packages, Redis dependency, and a bleeding `railway.toml` that injects its `buildCommand` into worker Dockerfiles. User deleted the Railway project and wants to START OVER with the simplest possible setup:

**Goal: one service. Next.js app → Supabase → Railway. Nothing else.**

Workers, BullMQ, Redis, node-cron, workspaces, testing infra — all out for now. Can add back later feature by feature when actually needed.

Model the setup on **Rankora** (working Stack A reference): single Next.js app, Dockerfile (not Nixpacks), standalone output, Supabase cloud. No workers, no workspace, no Redis.

---

## Current Problems (discovered in audit)

1. **`railway.toml` `buildCommand` bleeds into worker Dockerfiles** — the root cause of every failed Docker build. Railway injects the global build command into Docker-based services too.
2. **Workspace package (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`)** references 2 worker dirs that don't need to deploy.
3. **`lib/queue.ts`** is imported by 11 API routes — all non-critical (email sends, PDF generation, AI design, marketing). **None block auth/login/signup/dashboard.** Queue only fails when those specific routes are hit, not at boot.
4. **Nixpacks builder is fragile** — doesn't reliably run `postbuild` hook; doesn't cleanly handle our `cp` commands.
5. **Too many moving parts** — tests, scripts/vega-review, husky, lint-staged, sentry, upstash, pino-pretty etc. Each is one more thing that can break the build.

24	export function claudeSonnetCost(tokensInput: number, tokensOutput: number): TokenCost {
25	  const inputCents = Math.ceil((tokensInput / 1_000_000) * CLAUDE_SONNET_INPUT_CENTS_PER_MTOK)
26	  const outputCents = Math.ceil((tokensOutput / 1_000_000) * CLAUDE_SONNET_OUTPUT_CENTS_PER_MTOK)
27	  return { inputCents, outputCents, totalCents: inputCents + outputCents }
